purpose: Classify mortgages and registered charges affecting property title and separate the existence of security from enforcement, discharge and ownership consequences.
legal_distinctions: A mortgage or charge is a security interest and is not itself identical to ownership.
Registration of a charge is distinct from creation, transfer, redemption or discharge of the underlying security.
A judgment mortgage has its own statutory and procedural framework.
Mortgage enforcement is a separate legal stage from registration of the security.
A property sale does not automatically establish that a registered charge has been discharged.
Priority between interests may require separate title and registration analysis.
evidence_requirements: current folio_or_official registration evidence where registered
court order or judgment evidence where relevant
historical register evidence where the security predates current entries
official_routes: Tailte Éireann Land Registry registration services
Tailte Éireann forms and registration rules
Courts Service records where a court order or judgment mortgage is relevant
guardrails: Never treat a mortgage as proof of ownership.
Never state that a charge is discharged without supporting evidence.
Never infer enforcement merely from the existence of a charge.
Never infer priority without examining the applicable registration and priority framework.
Never convert a registration entry into a conclusion about the merits of an underlying debt dispute.
